name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Bennie Thompson running with $1.4M on hand
Republican challenger raised only ~$45K with no outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Thompson holds a D+11 seat with a large cash advantage over a barely funded challenger, and markets price his reelection near 97%. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the seat stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or a redistricting change to the district's boundaries would be the main thing to move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bennie Thompson, a longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Mississippi district that leans Democratic by about eleven points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.4 million on hand after raising about $770,000, while Republican Ron Eller has raised under $50,000 and shows no outside support. An independent candidate trails far behind in both money and profile.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Thompson's chances near 97%. The combination of the district's lean, incumbency, and a large financial gap points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty coming from turnout variation rather than any sign of a competitive race.
